Tig: text-mode interface for Git
=================================

What is Tig?
------------
Tig is an ncurses-based text-mode interface for git. It functions mainly
as a Git repository browser, but can also assist in staging changes for
commit at chunk level and act as a pager for output from various Git
commands.

Usage
-----

Basic usage examples:

	tig
	# Open Tig in the current repository

	tig log
	# Start in log view

	tig show
	# Open diff view

	tig blame <file>
	# Show file annotated by commits

	tig status
	# Start in status view

	tig grep <pattern>
	# Search for pattern in repository

	tig refs
	# Browse references (branches, tags)

	tig stash
	# Browse stash entries

	git show | tig
	# Use Tig as a pager

Views
-----

Tig presents various views of a repository:

- Main view: Shows a one line summary of each commit with author, date, and log message
- Log view: Presents a rich view of the revision log with full log message and diffstat
- Diff view: Shows the commit diff for the selected commit
- Blame view: Shows file annotated with commit information for each line
- Tree view: Shows the directory tree and file contents
- Refs view: Shows branches, tags, and other references
- Status view: Shows git-status output, allows staging/unstaging changes
- Stash view: Shows stash entries
- Grep view: Shows results from git-grep

Navigation
----------

- Arrow keys or k/j: Move up/down
- Enter: Open the selected item
- Tab: Switch between split views
- q: Close current view or quit
- h: Show help with all keybindings

Resources
---------

- Homepage: https://github.com/jonas/tig
- Manual: https://www.mankier.com/7/tigmanual

License
-------

See COPYING for license information.

======
:docext: adoc

NAME
----
tig - text-mode interface for Git

SYNOPSIS
--------
[verse]
_______________________________________________________________________
tig        [options] [revisions] [--] [paths]
tig log    [options] [revisions] [--] [paths]
tig show   [options] [revisions] [--] [paths]
tig reflog [options] [revisions]
tig blame  [options] [rev] [--] path
tig grep   [options] [pattern]
tig refs   [options]
tig stash  [options]
tig status
tig <      [Git command output]
_______________________________________________________________________

DESCRIPTION
-----------

Tig is an ncurses-based text-mode interface for git(1). It functions
mainly as a Git repository browser, but can also assist in staging
changes for commit at chunk level and act as a pager for output from
various Git commands.

OPTIONS
-------

Command line options recognized by Tig include all valid git-log(1) and
git-diff(1) options, as well as the following subcommands and Tig-specific
options. The first command line parameter not starting with "-" is interpreted
as being either a revision specification or a path and will end the option
parsing. All additional options will be passed to the underlying Git command.

Note that this means that any arguments to options should be specified
together. For example, run tig -Sfoo instead of tig -S foo, and tig --grep=foo
instead of tig --grep foo, otherwise foo will be interpreted as a revision
rather than an argument.

show::
	Open diff view using the given git-show(1) options.

blame::
	Show given file annotated by commits.
	Takes zero or more git-blame(1) options.
	Optionally limited from given revision.

status::
	Start up in status view.

log::
	Start up in log view, displaying git-log(1) output.

reflog::
	Start up in reflog view.

refs::
	Start up in refs view. All refs are displayed unless limited by using
	one of the '--branches', '--remotes', or '--tags' parameters.

stash::
	Start up in stash view.

grep::
	Open the grep view. Supports the same options as git-grep(1).

+<number>::
    Show the first view with line <number> visible and selected.

-v, --version::
	Show version and exit.

-h, --help::
	Show help message and exit.

-C <path>::
	Run as if Tig was started in <path> instead of the current working directory.

PAGER MODE
----------

Tig enters pager mode when input is provided via stdin and supports the
following subcommands and options:

--

 - When the 'show' subcommand is specified and the '--stdin' option is given,
   stdin is assumed to be a list of commit IDs and will be forwarded to the diff
   view's underlying git-show(1) command. For example:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ git rev-list --author=vivien HEAD | tig show --stdin
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 - When '--stdin' is given, stdin is assumed to be a list of commit IDs
   and will be forwarded to the main view's underlying git-log(1)
   command. For example:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --no-walk --stdin < cherry-picks.txt
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 - When '--pretty=raw' is given, stdin is assumed to be a "pretty=raw"
   formatted output similar to that of git-log(1). For example:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ git reflog --pretty=raw | tig --pretty=raw
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

--

When no subcommands nor options are given, the pager view will be used for
displaying the Git command input given on stdin. The pager view assumes the
input is either from git-log(1) or git-diff(1) and will highlight it similar to
the log and diff views. For example:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ git log -Schange -p --raw | tig
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

EXAMPLES
--------

Display the list of commits for the current branch:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Display commits from one or more branches:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig test master
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pretend as if all the refs in `refs/` are listed on the command line:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --all
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Display differences between two branches:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig test..master
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Display changes for sub-module versions:
---------

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
---------------------

In addition to environment variables used by Git (e.g. GIT_DIR), Tig defines
the ones below. The command related environment variables have access to the
internal state of Tig via replacement variables, such as `%(commit)` and
`%(blob)`.
ifdef::version[]
See manpage:tigrc[5] for a full list.
endif::version[]
ifndef::version[]
See link:tigrc.5.{docext}[tigrc(5)] for a full list.
endif::version[]

TIGRC_USER::
	Path of the user configuration file (defaults to `~/.tigrc` or
	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tig/config`).

TIGRC_SYSTEM::
	Path of the system wide configuration file (defaults to
	`{sysconfdir}/tigrc`). Define to empty string to use built-in
	configuration.

TIG_LS_REMOTE::
	Command for retrieving all repository references. The command
	should output data in the same format as git-ls-remote(1).

TIG_DIFF_OPTS::
	The diff options to use in the diff view. The diff view uses
	git-show(1) for formatting and always passes --patch-with-stat.  You
	may also set the `diff-options` setting in the configuration file.

TIG_TRACE::
	Path for trace file where information about Git commands are logged.

TIG_SCRIPT::
	Path to script that should be executed automatically on startup. If this
	environment variable is defined to the empty string, the script is read
	from stdin. The script is interpreted line-by-line and can contain
	prompt commands and key mappings. Note that the '<' character must be
	encoded as '<LT>' within the script.

	E.g. TIG_SCRIPT=<(echo :set main-view-commit-title-graph = no) tig

TIG_NO_DISPLAY::
	Open Tig without rendering anything to the terminal. This force Ncurses
	to write to /dev/null. The main use is for automated testing of Tig.

TIG_EDITOR::
	The editor command to use when visiting files. This environment
	variable overrides (in order of precedence) '$GIT_EDITOR',
	'core.editor' configuration, '$VISUAL' and '$EDITOR', so it
	allows to use a different editor from the one Git uses. The
	value is meant to be interpreted by the shell when it is used.

ifndef::doctype-manpage[]
The Tig Manual
==============
Jonas Fonseca <jonas.fonseca@gmail.com>
endif::doctype-manpage[]

This is the manual for Tig, the ncurses-based text-mode interface for git.
Tig allows you to browse changes in a Git repository and can additionally act
as a pager for output of various Git commands. When used as a pager, it will
display input from stdin and colorize it.

When browsing repositories, Tig uses the underlying Git commands to present
the user with various views, such as summarized commit log and showing the
commit with the log message, diffstat, and the diff.

ifdef::include-manual-toc[]
*Table of Contents*

include::manual.toc[]
endif::include-manual-toc[]

[[calling-conventions]]
Calling Conventions
-------------------

[[pager-mode]]
Pager Mode
~~~~~~~~~~

If stdin is a pipe, any log or diff options will be ignored and the pager view
will be opened loading data from stdin. The pager mode can be used for
colorizing output from various Git commands.

Example on how to colorize the output of git-show(1):

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ git show | tig
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[cmd-options]]
Git Command Options
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

All Git command options specified on the command line will be passed to the
given command and all will be shell quoted before they are passed to the
shell.

NOTE: If you specify options for the main view, you should not use the
`--pretty` option as this option will be set automatically to the format
expected by the main view.

Example on how to view a commit and show both author and committer
information:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig show --pretty=fuller
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

See the section on <<refspec, specifying revisions>> for an introduction to
revision options supported by the Git commands. For details on specific Git
command options, refer to the man page of the command in question.

[[viewer]]
The Viewer
----------

The display consists of a status window on the last line of the screen and one
or more views. The default is to only show one view at a time but it is
possible to split both the main and log view to also show the commit diff.

If you are in the log view and press 'Enter' when the current line is a commit
line, such as:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
commit 4d55caff4cc89335192f3e566004b4ceef572521
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

You will split the view so that the log view is displayed in the top window
and the diff view in the bottom window. You can switch between the two views
by pressing 'Tab'. To maximize the log view again, simply press 'l'.

[[views]]
Views
~~~~~

Various 'views' of a repository are presented. Each view is based on output
from an external command, most often 'git log', 'git diff', or 'git show'.

The main view::
	Is the default view, and it shows a one line summary of each commit
	in the chosen list of revisions. The summary includes committer or
	author date, author, committer, and the first line of the log message.
	Additionally, any repository references, such as tags, will be shown.

The log view::
	Presents a more rich view of the revision log showing the whole log
	message and the diffstat.

The reflog view::
	Presents a view of the reflog allowing to navigate the repo
	history.

The diff view::
	Shows either the diff of the current working tree, that is, what
	has changed since the last commit, or the commit diff complete
	with log message, diffstat and diff.

The tree view::
	Lists directory trees associated with the current revision allowing
	subdirectories to be descended or ascended and file blobs to be
	viewed.

The blob view::
	Displays the file content or "blob" of data associated with a file
	name.

The blame view::
	Displays the file content annotated or blamed by commits.

The refs view::
	Displays the branches, remotes and tags in the repository.

The status view::
	Displays status of files in the working tree and allows changes to be
	staged/unstaged as well as adding of untracked files.

The stage view::
	Displays diff changes for staged or unstaged files being tracked or
	file content of untracked files.

The stash view::
	Displays the list of stashes in the repository.

The grep view::
	Displays a list of files and all the lines that matches a search
	pattern.

The pager view::
	Is used for displaying both input from stdin and output from Git
	commands entered in the internal prompt.

The help view::
	Displays a quick reference of key bindings.

[[commit-id]]
Browsing State and User-defined Commands
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The viewer keeps track of both what head and commit ID you are currently
viewing. The commit ID will follow the cursor line and change every

making use of the options explained
in this section. For example, by configuring the environment variable
described in the section on <<diff-options, diff options>>.

[[path-limiting]]
Limit by Path Name
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

If you are interested only in those revisions that made changes to a specific
file (or even several files) list the files like this:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig Makefile README
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

To avoid ambiguity with Tig's subcommands or repository references such as tag
names, be sure to separate file names from other Git options using "`--`". So
if you have a file named 'status' it will clash with the 'status' subcommand,
and thus you will have to use:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig -- status
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[date-number-limiting]]
Limit by Date or Number
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

To speed up interaction with Git, you can limit the amount of commits to show
both for the log and main view. Either limit by date using e.g.
`--since=1.month` or limit by the number of commits using `-n400`.

If you are only interested in changes that happened between two dates you can
use:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --after="May 5th" --before="2006-05-16 15:44"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

NOTE: If you want to avoid having to quote dates containing spaces you can use
"." instead, e.g. `--after=May.5th`.

[[commit-range-limiting]]
Limiting by Commit Ranges
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Alternatively, commits can be limited to a specific range, such as "all
commits between 'tag-1.0' and 'tag-2.0'". For example:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig tag-1.0..tag-2.0
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

This way of commit limiting makes it trivial to only browse the commits which
haven't been pushed to a remote branch. Assuming 'origin' is your upstream
remote branch, using:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig origin..HEAD
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

will list what will be pushed to the remote branch. Optionally, the ending
'HEAD' can be left out since it is implied.

[[reachability-limiting]]
Limiting by Reachability
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Git interprets the range specifier "tag-1.0..tag-2.0" as "all commits
reachable from 'tag-2.0' but not from 'tag-1.0'".  Where reachability refers
to what commits are ancestors (or part of the history) of the branch or tagged
revision in question.

If you prefer to specify which commit to preview in this way use the
following:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig tag-2.0 ^tag-1.0
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

You can think of '^' as a negation operator. Using this alternate syntax, it
is possible to further prune commits by specifying multiple branch cut offs.

[[refspec-combi]]
Combining Revisions Specification
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Revision options can to some degree be combined, which makes it possible to
say "show at most 20 commits from within the last month that changed files
under the Documentation/ directory."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --since=1.month -n20 -- Documentation/
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[refspec-all]]
Examining All Repository References
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

In some cases, it can be useful to query changes across all references in a
repository. An example is to ask "did any line of development in this
repository change a particular file within the last week". This can be
accomplished using:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --all --since=1.week -- Makefile
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

about new releases and how to report bugs and feature requests.

tigrc(5)
========
:docext: adoc

NAME
----
tigrc - Tig configuration file


SYNOPSIS
--------
[verse]
_______________________________________________________________________
*set*   'variable' *=* 'value'
*bind*  'keymap' 'key' 'action'
*color* 'area' 'fgcolor' 'bgcolor' '[attributes]'
*source* 'path'
_______________________________________________________________________


DESCRIPTION
-----------

You can permanently set an option by putting it in the `~/.tigrc` file.  The
file consists of a series of 'commands'.  Each line of the file may contain
only one command.  Commands can span multiple lines if each line is
terminated by a backslash ('\') character. 

The hash mark ('#') is used as a 'comment' character. All text after the
comment character to the end of the line is ignored. You can use comments to
annotate your initialization file.

Certain options can be manipulated at runtime via the option menu. In
addition, options can also be toggled with the `:toggle` prompt command
or by entering the configuration command into the prompt.

In some environments, a user's configuration will be stored in the alternate
location `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tig/config`.  For brevity, this document will
refer only to `~/.tigrc`.

Git configuration
-----------------

Alternatively to using `~/.tigrc`, Tig options can be set by putting them in
one of the Git configuration files, which are read by Tig on startup. See
'git-config(1)' for which files to use. The following example show the basic
syntax to use for settings, bindings and colors.

// TEST: gitconfig
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tig] show-changes = true
[tig "color"] cursor = yellow red bold 
[tig "bind"] generic = P parent
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

In addition to tig-specific options, the following Git options are read from
the Git configuration:

'color.*'::

	Colors for the various UI types. Can be configured via the 'git-colors'
	setting.

'core.abbrev'::

	The width of the commit ID. See also 'id-width' option.

'core.editor'::

	The editor command. Can be overridden by setting TIG_EDITOR or
	GIT_EDITOR.

'core.worktree'::

	The path to the root of the working tree.

'gui.encoding'::

	The encoding to use for displaying of file content.

'i18n.commitencoding'::

	The encoding used for commits. The default is UTF-8.

Set command
-----------

A few selective variables can be configured via the set command. The syntax
is:

[verse]
*set* variables *=* value

Examples:

// TEST: tigrc
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
set commit-order = topo		# Order commits topologically
set git-colors = no		# Do not read Git's color settings.
set horizontal-scroll = 33%	# Scroll 33% of the view width
set blame-options = -C -C -C	# Blame lines from other files

# Wrap branch names with () and tags with <>
set reference-format = (branch) <tag>

# Configure blame view columns using command spanning multiple lines.
set blame-view = \
	date:default \
	author:abbreviated \
	committer:abbreviated \
	file-name:auto \
	id:yes,color \
	line-number:yes,interval=5 text
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Or in the Git configuration files:

// TEST: gitconfig
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tig]
	line-graphics = no	# Disable graphics characters
	tab-size = 8		# Number of spaces per tab
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

The type of variables is either bool, int, string, or mixed.

Valid bool values::

	To set a bool variable to true use either "1", "true", or "yes".
	Any other value will set the variable to false.

Valid int values::

	A non-negative integer.

Valid string values::

	A string of characters. Optionally, use either ' or " as delimiters.

Valid mixed values::

	These values are composites of the above types. The valid values are
	specified in the description.

'log-options' (string)::

	A space-separated string of default options that should be passed to the
	git-log(1) command used by the log view. Options can be overridden by

View settings
~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The view settings define the order and options for the different columns of a
view. Each view setting expects a space-separated list of column specifications.
Column specifications starts with the column type, and can optionally be
followed by a colon (`:`) and a list of column options. E.g. the following
column specification defines an 'author' column displaying the author email and
with a fixed width of 20 characters: `author:email,width=20`.

The first option value in a column specification is always the 'display' option.
When no 'display' value is given, 'yes' is assumed. For 'display' options
expecting an enumerated value this will automatically resolve to the default
enum value. For example, `file-name` will automatically have its 'display'
setting resolve to 'auto'.

Specifications can also be given for a single column, for example to override
the defaults in the system tigrc file. To override a single column, use the
column name as a suffix after the view setting name, e.g. `main-view-date` will
allow to set the date in the main view.

set pager-view = line-number:yes,interval=10 text

set main-view-date = custom
set main-view-date-format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"
set blame-view-line-number = no
# Use Git's default commit order, even when the commit graph is enabled.
set commit-order = default

bind generic G none

bind status + !git commit --amend

Advanced shell-like commands
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

If your command requires use of dynamic features, such as subshells,
expansion of environment variables and process control, this can be achieved by
using a shell command:

.Configure a binding to copy the current commit ID to the clipboard.
// TEST: tigrc

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Or by using a combination of Git aliases and Tig external commands. The
following example entries can be put in either the .gitconfig or .git/config
file:

.Git configuration which binds Tig keys to Git command aliases.
// TEST: gitconfig
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

	generic = V @git gitk-bg
	generic = > !git publish

Internal user-defined commands
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Actions beginning with a ':' will be run and interpreted as internal commands
and act similar to commands run via Tig's prompt. Valid internal commands are
configuration file options (as described in this document) and pager view
commands. Examples:

// TEST: tigrc
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reload ~/.tigrc when 'S' is pressed
bind generic S :source .tigrc

# Change diff view to show all commit changes regardless of file limitations
bind diff F :set diff-options = --full-diff

# Show the output of git-reflog(1) in the pager view
bind generic W :!git reflog

# Search for previous diff (c)hunk and next diff header
bind stage 2 :?^@@
bind stage D :/^diff --(git|cc)

bind main I :toggle id				# Show/hide the ID column
bind diff D :toggle diff-options --minimal	# Use minimal diff algorithm
bind diff [ :toggle diff-context -3		# Decrease context (-U arg)
bind diff ] :toggle diff-context +3		# Increase context
bind generic V :toggle split-view-height -10%	# Decrease split height
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

that will be substituted before the command is run.

Highlighting
~~~~~~~~~~~~

--

Diff markup::

Options concerning diff start, chunks and lines added and deleted.

*diff-header*, *diff-chunk*, *diff-stat*, *diff-add*, *diff-add2*,
*diff-del*, *diff-del2*, *diff-add-highlight*, *diff-del-highlight*

Enhanced Git diff markup::

Extra diff information emitted by the Git diff machinery, such as mode
changes, rename detection, and similarity.

*diff-oldmode*, *diff-newmode*, *diff-copy-from*, *diff-copy-to*,
*diff-similarity*, *diff-index*

Pretty print commit headers::

Commit diffs and the revision logs are usually formatted using pretty printed
headers , unless `--pretty=raw` was given. This includes lines, such as merge
info, commit ID, and author and committer date.

*pp-refs*, *pp-reflog*, *pp-reflogmsg*, *pp-merge*

Raw commit header::

Usually shown when `--pretty=raw` is given, however 'commit' is pretty much
omnipresent.

*commit*, *parent*, *tree*, *author*, *committer*

Commit message::

Most common trailer lines (e.g. `Signed-off-by`) are colorized.
Characters in the commit title exceeding a predefined width can be highlighted.


Tree markup::

Colors for information of the tree view.

*tree-dir*, *tree-file*

Source command
-------------

Source commands make it possible to read additional configuration files.
Sourced files are included in-place, meaning when a 'source' command is
encountered the file will be immediately read. Any commands later in the
current configuration file will take precedence.

If the given path does not exist, tig will proceed with a warning. Give
the `-q` parameter to suppress the warning.

The syntax is:

[verse]
*source* '[-q]' 'path'

Examples:
// TEST: tigrc
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
source ~/.tig/colorscheme.tigrc
source ~/.tig/keybindings.tigrc

ifndef::doctype-manpage[]
The Tig Manual
==============
Jonas Fonseca <jonas.fonseca@gmail.com>
endif::doctype-manpage[]

This is the manual for Tig, the ncurses-based text-mode interface for git.
Tig allows you to browse changes in a Git repository and can additionally act
as a pager for output of various Git commands. When used as a pager, it will
display input from stdin and colorize it.

When browsing repositories, Tig uses the underlying Git commands to present
the user with various views, such as summarized commit log and showing the
commit with the log message, diffstat, and the diff.

ifdef::include-manual-toc[]
*Table of Contents*

include::manual.toc[]
endif::include-manual-toc[]

[[calling-conventions]]
Calling Conventions
-------------------

[[pager-mode]]
Pager Mode
~~~~~~~~~~

If stdin is a pipe, any log or diff options will be ignored and the pager view
will be opened loading data from stdin. The pager mode can be used for
colorizing output from various Git commands.

Example on how to colorize the output of git-show(1):

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ git show | tig
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[cmd-options]]
Git Command Options
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

All Git command options specified on the command line will be passed to the
given command and all will be shell quoted before they are passed to the
shell.

NOTE: If you specify options for the main view, you should not use the
`--pretty` option as this option will be set automatically to the format
expected by the main view.

Example on how to view a commit and show both author and committer
information:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig show --pretty=fuller
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

See the section on <<refspec, specifying revisions>> for an introduction to
revision options supported by the Git commands. For details on specific Git
command options, refer to the man page of the command in question.

[[viewer]]
The Viewer
----------

The display consists of a status window on the last line of the screen and one
or more views. The default is to only show one view at a time but it is
possible to split both the main and log view to also show the commit diff.

If you are in the log view and press 'Enter' when the current line is a commit
line, such as:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
commit 4d55caff4cc89335192f3e566004b4ceef572521
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

You will split the view so that the log view is displayed in the top window
and the diff view in the bottom window. You can switch between the two views
by pressing 'Tab'. To maximize the log view again, simply press 'l'.

[[views]]
Views
~~~~~

Various 'views' of a repository are presented. Each view is based on output
from an external command, most often 'git log', 'git diff', or 'git show'.

The main view::
	Is the default view, and it shows a one line summary of each commit
	in the chosen list of revisions. The summary includes committer or
	author date, author, committer, and the first line of the log message.
	Additionally, any repository references, such as tags, will be shown.

The log view::
	Presents a more rich view of the revision log showing the whole log
	message and the diffstat.

The reflog view::
	Presents a view of the reflog allowing to navigate the repo
	history.

The diff view::
	Shows either the diff of the current working tree, that is, what
	has changed since the last commit, or the commit diff complete
	with log message, diffstat and diff.

The tree view::
	Lists directory trees associated with the current revision allowing
	subdirectories to be descended or ascended and file blobs to be
	viewed.

The blob view::
	Displays the file content or "blob" of dat

Example user-defined commands:

 - Allow to amend the last commit:

	bind generic + !git commit --amend

 - Copy commit ID to clipboard:

	bind generic 9 @sh -c "echo -n %(commit) | xclip -selection c"

 - Add/edit notes for the current commit used during a review:

	bind generic T !git notes edit %(commit)

 - Enter Git's interactive add for fine-grained staging of file content:

	bind generic I !git add -i %(file)

 - Rebase current branch on top of the selected branch:

	bind refs 3 !git rebase -i %(branch)

[[title-window]]
Title Windows
~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Each view has a title window which shows the name of the view, current commit
ID if available, and where the view is positioned:

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[main] c622eefaa485995320bc743431bae0d497b1d875 - commit 1 of 61             1%
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By default, the title of the current view is highlighted using bold font.  For
long loading views (taking over 3 seconds) the time since loading started will
be appended:

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[main] 77d9e40fbcea3238015aea403e06f61542df9a31 - commit 1 of 779 loading 5s 0%
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[env-variables]]
Environment Variables
---------------------

Several options related to the interface with Git can be configured via
environment options.

[[configuration-files]]
Configuration Files
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Upon startup, Tig first reads the system wide configuration file
(`{sysconfdir}/tigrc` by default) and then proceeds to read the user's
configuration file (`~/.tigrc` or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tig/config` by default).
The paths to either of these files can be overridden through the following
environment variables:

TIGRC_USER::
	Path of the user configuration file.

TIGRC_SYSTEM::
	Path of the system wide configuration file.

[[history-files]]
History Files
~~~~~~~~~~~~~

If compiled with readline support, Tig writes a persistent command and search
history to `~/.tig_history` or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/tig/history`.

[[repo-refs]]
Repository References
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Commits that are referenced by tags and branch heads will be marked by the
reference name surrounded by '[' and ']':

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
2006-03-26 19:42 Petr Baudis         | [cogito-0.17.1] Cogito 0.17.1
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you want to limit what branches are shown, say only show branches named
`master` or those which start with the `feature/` prefix, you can do it by setting
the following variable:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ TIG_LS_REMOTE="git ls-remote . master feature/*" tig
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Or set the variable permanently in your environment.

--

TIG_LS_REMOTE::

	Command for retrieving all repository references. The command should
	output data in the same format as git-ls-remote(1). Defaults to:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
git ls-remote .
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

--

[[diff-options]]
Diff options
~~~~~~~~~~~~

It is possible to alter how diffs are shown by the diff view. If for example
you prefer to have commit and author dates shown as relative dates, use:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ TIG_DIFF_OPTS="--relative-date" tig
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Or set the variable permanently in your environment.

-------------------

[[path-limiting]]
Limit by Path Name
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

If you are interested only in those revisions that made changes to a specific
file (or even several files) list the files like this:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig Makefile README
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

To avoid ambiguity with Tig's subcommands or repository references such as tag
names, be sure to separate file names from other Git options using "`--`". So
if you have a file named 'status' it will clash with the 'status' subcommand,
and thus you will have to use:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig -- status
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[date-number-limiting]]
Limit by Date or Number
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

To speed up interaction with Git, you can limit the amount of commits to show
both for the log and main view. Either limit by date using e.g.
`--since=1.month` or limit by the number of commits using `-n400`.

If you are only interested in changes that happened between two dates you can
use:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --after="May 5th" --before="2006-05-16 15:44"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

NOTE: If you want to avoid having to quote dates containing spaces you can use
"." instead, e.g. `--after=May.5th`.

[[commit-range-limiting]]
Limiting by Commit Ranges
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Alternatively, commits can be limited to a specific range, such as "all
commits between 'tag-1.0' and 'tag-2.0'". For example:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig tag-1.0..tag-2.0
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

This way of commit limiting makes it trivial to only browse the commits which
haven't been pushed to a remote branch. Assuming 'origin' is your upstream
remote branch, using:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig origin..HEAD
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

will list what will be pushed to the remote branch. Optionally, the ending
'HEAD' can be left out since it is implied.

[[reachability-limiting]]
Limiting by Reachability
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Git interprets the range specifier "tag-1.0..tag-2.0" as "all commits
reachable from 'tag-2.0' but not from 'tag-1.0'".  Where reachability refers
to what commits are ancestors (or part of the history) of the branch or tagged
revision in question.

If you prefer to specify which commit to preview in this way use the
following:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig tag-2.0 ^tag-1.0
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

You can think of '^' as a negation operator. Using this alternate syntax, it
is possible to further prune commits by specifying multiple branch cut offs.

[[refspec-combi]]
Combining Revisions Specification
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Revision options can to some degree be combined, which makes it possible to
say "show at most 20 commits from within the last month that changed files
under the Documentation/ directory."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --since=1.month -n20 -- Documentation/
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[refspec-all]]
Examining All Repository References
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

In some cases, it can be useful to query changes across all references in a
repository. An example is to ask "did any line of development in this
repository change a particular file within the last week". This can be
accomplished using:

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ tig --all --since=1.week -- Makefile
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

import subprocess,time,os,sys
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def trace(args, cwd="/tmp/t1", keys_script=":quit\n", stdin_data=None, env_extra=None):
    open("/tmp/s.tig","w").write(keys_script)
    try: os.remove("/tmp/trace.log")
    except: pass
    sess="sx"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",sess],capture_output=True)
    envstr=""
    if env_extra:
        envstr=" ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k,v in env_extra.items())+" "
    if stdin_data is not None:
        # write to file and pipe
        open("/tmp/in.txt","w").write(stdin_data)
        cmd=f"cd {cwd} && {envstr}TIG_TRACE=/tmp/trace.log TIG_SCRIPT=/tmp/s.tig {EXE} {args} < /tmp/in.txt; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 5"
    else:
        cmd=f"cd {cwd} && {envstr}TIG_TRACE=/tmp/trace.log TIG_SCRIPT=/tmp/s.tig {EXE} {args}; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 5"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",sess,"-x","200","-y","50",cmd])
    time.sleep(1.2)
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",sess,"-p"],capture_output=True,text=True)

    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",sess],capture_output=True)

    print(f"=== ARGS {args} cwd={cwd} stdin={stdin_data!r} ===")

import subprocess,time,os
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run_typing(cwd,args,typing=None,keys=None,size=(80,24),env=None):
    sess="st"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",sess],capture_output=True)
    envstr=""
    if env: envstr=" ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k,v in env.items())+" "
    cmd=f"cd {cwd} && {envstr}TERM=xterm-256color {EXE} {args}; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 100"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",sess,"-x",str(size[0]),"-y",str(size[1]),cmd])
    time.sleep(0.7)
    def snap(label=""):
        r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",sess,"-p"],capture_output=True,text=True)
        print(label); print(r.stdout); print("===")
    snap("initial")
    if typing:
        for txt,enter in typing:
            subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,"-l",txt])
            if enter: subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,"Enter"])
            time.sleep(0.4); snap(f"after {txt!r}")
    if keys:
        for k in keys:
            subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,k]); time.sleep(0.3); snap(f"key {k}")
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",sess],capture_output=True)
PY

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from type import run_typing

~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The view settings define the order and options for the different columns of a
view. Each view setting expects a space-separated list of column specifications.
Column specifications starts with the column type, and can optionally be
followed by a colon (`:`) and a list of column options. E.g. the following
column specification defines an 'author' column displaying the author email and
with a fixed width of 20 characters: `author:email,width=20`.

The first option value in a column specification is always the 'display' option.
When no 'display' value is given, 'yes' is assumed. For 'display' options
expecting an enumerated value this will automatically resolve to the default
enum value. For example, `file-name` will automatically have its 'display'
setting resolve to 'auto'.

Specifications can also be given for a single column, for example to override
the defaults in the system tigrc file. To override a single column, use the
column name as a suffix after the view setting name, e.g. `main-view-date` will
allow to set the date in the main view.

Keys are mapped by first searching the keybindings for the current view, then
the keybindings for the *generic* keymap, and last the default keybindings.
Thus, the view keybindings override the generic keybindings which override the
built-in keybindings.

Clear keybinding (unbind) from all keymaps at once with bind *generic* 'key'
*none*.

Keybindings at the line-entry prompt are typically governed by the readline
library, and are configured separately in `~/.inputrc`.  See 'readline(1)'.
Tig respects but does not require an `$if tig` section in `~/.inputrc`.

--

Keymaps::

Valid keymaps are: *main*, *diff*, *log*, *reflog*, *help*, *pager*, *status*,
*stage*, *tree*, *blob*, *blame*, *refs*, *stash*, *grep* and *generic*. Use
*generic* to set key mapping in all keymaps (which may still be overridden by a
specific view keybinding). Use *search* to define keys for navigating search
results during search.

Key values::

Key values should never be quoted. Use either an ASCII or UTF8-encoded character
or one of the following symbolic key names. Symbolic key names are case
insensitive and starts with "<" and ends with ">". Use *<Hash>* to bind to the
`#` key, since the hash mark is used as a comment character. Use *<LessThan>* to
bind to the `<` key.

*<Enter>*, *<Space>*, *<Backspace>*, *<Tab>*, *<Escape>* or *<Esc>*, *<Left>*,
*<Right>*, *<Up>*, *<Down>*, *<Insert>* or *<Ins>*, *<Delete>* or *<Del>*,
*<Hash>*, *<LessThan>* or *<LT>*, *<Home>*, *<End>*, *<PageUp>* or *<PgUp>*,
*<PageDown>* or *<PgDown>*, *<ScrollBack>* or *<SBack>*, *<ScrollFwd>* or
*<SFwd>*, *<ShiftTab>* or *<BackTab>*, *<ShiftLeft>*, *<ShiftRight>*,
*<ShiftDelete>* or *<ShiftDel>*, *<ShiftHome>*, *<ShiftEnd>*, *<SingleQuote>*,
*<DoubleQuote>*, *<F1>* ... *<F19>*

To define key mappings with the `Ctrl` key, use `<Ctrl-key>`. In addition, key
combos consisting of an initial `Escape` key followed by a normal key value can
be bound using `<Esc>key`.

Examples:
// TEST: tigrc
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
bind main R		refresh
bind main <Down>	next
bind main <Ctrl-f>	scroll-page-down
bind main <Esc>o	options
bind main <ShiftTab>	parent
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Notes

- Tig reads keystrokes via ncurses and is subject to various limitations. See
  'ncurses(3x)' and 'terminfo(5)' (or termcap).

- `Ctrl-m` and `Ctrl-i` cannot be bound as they conflict with 'Enter' and 'Tab'
  respectively.

- Case differences cannot be distinguished in control sequences such as
 `Ctrl-f` and `Ctrl-F`.

- `Ctrl-<Space>` is typically translated to `Ctrl-@`, which is available for
  binding.

- Only some subset of special symbolic keys such as `<ShiftTab>` will be
  available in any given terminal emulator.

- `Ctrl-z` is automatically used for process control and will suspend Tig and
  open a subshell (use `fg` to reenter Tig).

Actions::

Actions are either specified as user-defined commands (external or internal) or
using action names as described in the following sections.

--

External user-defined command
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

These actions start with one or more of the following option flags followed by
the command that should be executed.

[frame="none",grid="none",cols="25<m,75<"]
|=============================================================================
|!			|Run the command in the foreground with output shown.
|@			|Run the command in the background with no output.
|+			|Run the command synchronously, and echo the first line
			 of output to the status bar.
|?			|Prompt the user before executing the command.
|<			|Exit Tig after executing the command.
|>			|Re-open Tig instantly in the last displayed view after
			 executing the command.
|=============================================================================

Unless otherwise specified, commands are run in the foreground with their
console output shown (as if '!' was specified). When multiple command options
are specified their behavior are combined, e.g. "?<git commit" will prompt the
user whether to execute the command and will exit Tig after completion.

Note that if you want to use pipes or redirection in your commands then you
must run them in a subshell, i.e. embed your commands in `sh -c '<commands>'`.

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

User-defined commands can optionally refer to Tig's internal state using the

def str_width(s):
    w=0
    for ch in s:
        if ch in (G_VLINE,G_HLINE,G_UR,G_LR,G_UL,G_LL,G_LTEE,G_RTEE,G_TTEE,G_BTEE,G_CROSS,G_COMMIT,G_MERGE,G_ROOT):
            w+=1
        elif ord(ch)<32:
            continue
        elif unicodedata.combining(ch):
            continue
        elif unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch) in ('W','F'):
            w+=2
        else:
            w+=1
    return w

def truncate_str(s,width,delim="~"):
    if str_width(s)<=width:
        return s
    if width<=0:
        return ""
    # keep width-1 chars incl wide handling simply char by char
    out=[]; w=0
    for ch in s:
        cw=str_width(ch)
        if w+cw>width-1:
            break
        out.append(ch); w+=cw
    out.append(delim)
    return "".join(out)

def pad_str(s,width):
    w=str_width(s)
    if w>=width:
        return truncate_str(s,width) if w>width else s

    if "\t" not in s:

    out=[]; col=0

        if ch=="\t":

            out.append(" "*n); col+=n
        else:
            out.append(ch); col+=str_width(ch)

    # args list, returns (rc, stdout_bytes, stderr_bytes)
    if trace:

def expand_range_token(tok):
    # return list expanded via git rev-parse --symbolic --revs-only tok, if contains ..
    if '..' not in tok:
        return [tok]
    rc,out,err=git_text(["rev-parse","--symbolic","--revs-only",tok],trace=False)
    if rc==0:
        lines=[l for l in out.splitlines() if l]
        if lines:
            return lines
    return [tok]

def partitioned_args(app,args):
    # args may contain '--'
    if '--' in args:
        idx=args.index('--')
        left=args[:idx]; files=args[idx+1:]
        user=[]
        for tok in left:
            user.extend(expand_range_token(tok))
        return user,files,left
    else:
        # files identified via app.file_args computed earlier (output lines)
        files=app._parsed_files if hasattr(app,'_parsed_files') else []
        user=[]
        for tok in args:
            if tok in files:
                continue
            user.extend(expand_range_token(tok))
        return user,files,args

            raw=raw[:-1]
        for i,line in enumerate(raw):

            if line.endswith('\r'): line=line[:-1]
            vl=VLine(expand_tabs(line,self.opts.int_opt('tab-size',8)))

            if commit_map:

            self.lines.append(vl)

        show_lineno=False; interval=5
        for c in cols:

                if is_column_shown(c): show_lineno=True
                try: interval=int(c.opt('interval','5'))
                except: interval=5
        prefix=""
        if show_lineno:
            maxln=len(self.lines)
            w=max(3,len(str(maxln)))
            if line.lineno%interval==0 or line.lineno==1:
                prefix=str(line.lineno).rjust(w)+G_VLINE+" "
            else:
                prefix=" "*w+G_VLINE+" "
        # search highlight handled by app by splitting? Color per classification
        color=classify_text_line(line.text,self.name)

            m=re.match(r'^(\s*\S.*?)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s+([+-]*)\s*$',line.text)

                if plus: segs.append((plus,'diff-add',0))

    def _graph_enabled(self):

def expand_range_token(tok):
    # return list expanded via git rev-parse --symbolic --revs-only tok, if contains ..
    if '..' not in tok:
        return [tok]
    rc,out,err=git_text(["rev-parse","--symbolic","--revs-only",tok],trace=False)
    if rc==0:
        lines=[l for l in out.splitlines() if l]
        if lines:
            return lines
    return [tok]

def partitioned_args(app,args):
    # args may contain '--'
    if '--' in args:
        idx=args.index('--')
        left=args[:idx]; files=args[idx+1:]
        user=[]
        for tok in left:
            user.extend(expand_range_token(tok))
        return user,files,left
    else:
        # files identified via app.file_args computed earlier (output lines)
        files=app._parsed_files if hasattr(app,'_parsed_files') else []
        user=[]
        for tok in args:
            if tok in files:
                continue
            user.extend(expand_range_token(tok))
        return user,files,args

def expand_range_token(tok):
    # return list expanded via git rev-parse --symbolic --revs-only tok, if contains ..
    if '..' not in tok:
        return [tok]
    rc,out,err=git_text(["rev-parse","--symbolic","--revs-only",tok],trace=False)
    if rc==0:
        lines=[l for l in out.splitlines() if l]
        if lines:
            return lines
    return [tok]

def partitioned_args(app,args):
    # args may contain '--'
    if '--' in args:
        idx=args.index('--')
        left=args[:idx]; files=args[idx+1:]
        user=[]
        for tok in left:
            user.extend(expand_range_token(tok))
        return user,files,left
    else:
        # files identified via app.file_args computed earlier (output lines)
        files=app._parsed_files if hasattr(app,'_parsed_files') else []
        user=[]
        for tok in args:
            if tok in files:

            if not is_stdin: args+=["--"]
            else: args+=["--"]
        rc,txt=run_git(args,input_data=stdin_data,merge_stderr=True)
        txt=txt.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
        self.set_text(txt)
        self._post()
        # describe for default HEAD case when no explicit commit
        if not self.commit_arg and not self.raw_args and self.repo and self.repo.is_repo:
            desc=self.repo.describe("HEAD")
            if desc:
                self._describe=desc
            else: self._describe=None
        elif self.commit_arg and self.repo:
            # when diff opened for a specific commit via Enter, does tig describe? trace for split diff didn't show describe. Skip.
            self._describe=None
        else:
            self._describe=None
        # Insert/amend Refs line ? Tig's UI rendering adds (?) The git show output doesn't contain Refs: Tig inserts it when rendering? In set_text lines, second line is Refs: . That is synthesized by tig parsing commit and refs.
        self._insert_refs()
    def _insert_refs(self):
        if not self.lines: return
        # Find commit line
        for i,vl in enumerate(self.lines[:3]):
            m=re.match(r'commit ([0-9a-f]{7,64})',vl.text)
            if m:
                commit=m.group(1)
                if self.repo:
                    refs=self.repo.refs_for(commit,self.opts)
                    ref_strs=[f for f,r in refs]
                    # describe extra only if _describe
                    if getattr(self,'_describe',None):
                        ref_strs.append(self._describe)
                    if ref_strs:
                        # check if next line already Refs:
                        if i+1>=len(self.lines) or not self.lines[i+1].text.startswith('Refs:'):
                            vl2=VLine("Refs: "+", ".join(ref_strs),commit=commit,lineno=0)
                            self.lines.insert(i+1,vl2)
                            # renumber lineno for line-number column (original line numbers based on position)
                            for idx,l in enumerate(self.lines): l.lineno=idx+1
                break
    def _diff_worktree(self,staged):
        # For main pseudo staged/unstaged, diff view behaviour is actually stage view in original. But DiffView opened from ??? stage pseudo via main Enter shows StageView (handled by app). This method used if diff directly for working tree (view-diff key 'd' in main with no commit?)
        args=["diff","--encoding=UTF-8","--no-color","--stat=200","--patch-with-stat"] if False else None
        # original 'd' on an unstaged pseudo uses stage; on a real commit uses show. Working tree diff via git diff:
        if staged:
            gitargs=["diff","--cached","--no-color","--patch-with-stat","--stat=200"]
        else:
            gitargs=["diff","--no-color","--patch-with-stat","--stat=200"]
        ctx=self.opts.get('diff-context','3')
        try: ctxi=int(ctx)
        except: ctxi=3
        if ctxi!=3: gitargs.append(f"-U{ctxi}")
        gitargs+=["--"]
        rc,out,err=run_git(gitargs,merge_stderr=True)
        return out.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
    def _post(self):
        cur=self.commit_arg or ""
        self._file_by_line=[]
        curfile=""
        for vl in self.lines:
            m=re.match(r'commit ([0-9a-f]{7,64})',vl.text)
            if m: cur=m.group(1); vl.commit=cur
            elif cur: vl.commit=cur
            dm=re.match(r'diff --git a/(.*?) b/(.*)',vl.text)
            if dm: curfile=dm.group(2)
            vl.file=curfile
        if self.lines and cur: self.title_info=cur
    def _title_info(self):
        # special for staged/unstaged? Diff view for a commit uses commit hash. If lines start with ... no commit (worktree diff) return special prompt string handled in title()
        if self.unstaged or self.staged:
            return ""
        l=self.current_line()
        if l and l.commit: return l.commit
        return self.title_info
    def title(self):
        if self.unstaged or self.staged:
            # If this is used as stage-like? original diff for worktree? It shows Press ... as info.
            # Determine based on current line's file/diff position
            l=self.current_line()
            total=len(self.lines)
            if total==0: return f"[{self.name}]"
            # If current line is after diff --git for a file, show ...?
            # Use stage-like logic in StageView; here fallback
            return f"[{self.name}] Press '<Enter>' to jump to file diff - line {self.selected+1} of {total}"
        return super().title()

class StageView(DiffView):
    name="stage"
    def __init__(self,app, staged=False, unstaged=False, untracked_file=None, file=None, section=None):
        super().__init__(app,commit=None,staged=staged,unstaged=unstaged,untracked_file=untracked_file)
        self.is_stage=True
        self.only_file=file
        self.section=section  # 'staged','unstaged','untracked'
        if untracked_file: self.section='untracked'
        elif staged: self.section='staged'
        elif unstaged: self.section='unstaged'
    def load(self):
        self.loaded=True
        if self.section=='untracked' and self.only_file:
            try: txt=open(self.only_file,encoding='utf-8',errors='surrogateescape').read()
            except Exception as e: txt=""
            self.set_text(txt); self._post_stage(); return
        if self.section=='untracked' and not self.only_file:
            # all untracked files content? tig stage for untracked section shows file contents concatenated? Test: enter on untracked header – it showed ??? earlier untracked section stage? We entered unstaged header. Need approximate: show contents of each untracked file?
            # Use git ls-files others
            rc,out,err=git_text(["ls-files","--others","--exclude-standard","-z"])
            files=[f for f in out.split('\x00') if f]
            txt=""
            for f in files:
                try: txt+=open(f,errors='surrogateescape').read()
                except: pass
            self.set_text(txt); self._post_stage(); return
        staged=(self.section=='staged')
        gitargs=["diff","--no-color"]
        if staged: gitargs.append("--cached")
        gitargs+=["--patch-with-stat","--stat=200"]
        try: ctxi=int(self.opts.get('diff-context','3'))
        except: ctxi=3
        if ctxi!=3: gitargs.append(f"-U{ctxi}")
        ispace=str(self.opts.get('ignore-space','no')).lower()
        if ispace in ('all','yes','true'): gitargs+=["--ignore-all-space"]
        elif ispace=='some': gitargs+=["--ignore-space-change"]
        elif ispace=='at-eol': gitargs+=["--ignore-space-at-eol"]
        gitargs+=["--"]
        if self.only_file: gitargs+=[self.only_file]
        rc,out,err=run_git(gitargs,merge_stderr=True)
        txt=out.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
        # If file is untracked but only_file set without section untracked – caller sets
        self.set_text(txt); self._post_stage()
    def _post_stage(self):
        curfile=""
        for vl in self.lines:
            dm=re.match(r'diff --git a/(.*?) b/(.*)',vl.text)
            if dm: curfile=dm.group(2)
            vl.file=curfile
    def title(self):
        total=len(self.lines)
        if total==0: return "[stage]"
        l=self.current_line()
        # If selected line is in a diff for a file (after diff header?) or diff header itself?
        # Original: line 1 (stat file line) -> "Press '<Enter>' to jump to file diff"
        # line of "diff --git" (?) or its following? earlier selecting line 4 (index line?) gave "Unstaged changes to 'file.txt'"
        # Determine: if the current line is a diff line (index >= first diff --git line) and file known, show "<Section> changes to '<file>'"
        # else press...
        if l and l.file:
            # check if selected index >= position of that file's diff header
            # find header index for this file
            # If current line text starts with space filename in stat area (before diff), then press...
            # Stat lines are before first diff --git; those lines have file="" assigned in _post (since curfile resets only after header) – good because we set vl.file only after header encountered; stat lines have ""
            secname={'staged':'Staged','unstaged':'Unstaged','untracked':'Untracked'}.get(self.section,'Unstaged')
            return f"[stage] {secname} changes to '{l.file}' - line {self.selected+1} of {total}"
        return f"[stage] Press '<Enter>' to jump to file diff - line {self.selected+1} of {total}"

class PagerView(TextView):
    name="pager"
    def __init__(self,app,text="",title_info=""):
        super().__init__(app); self._text=text; self.title_info=title_info
    def load(self):
        self.loaded=True
        self.set_text(self._text)
        self._post()
    def _post(self):
        cur=""
        for vl in self.lines:
            m=re.match(r'commit ([0-9a-f]{7,64})',vl.text)
            if m: cur=m.group(1); vl.commit=cur
            elif cur: vl.commit=cur
            dm=re.match(r'diff --git a/(.*?) b/(.*)',vl.text)
            if dm: vl.file=dm.group(2)
        if cur and not self.title_info: self.title_info=cur
    def _title_info(self):
        # pager title in original: if no commit, empty => "[pager] - line..."
        # If stdin was git log with commits, maybe title shows commit? Let's keep current commit if line has one else ""
        l=self.current_line()
        if l and l.commit: return l.commit
        return ""

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

For more custom needs, external commands provide a way to easily execute
a script or program. They are bound to keys and use information from the
current browsing state, such as the current commit ID. Tig comes with
the following built-in external commands:

Revision Specification
----------------------

This section describes various ways to specify what revisions to display or
otherwise limit the view to. Tig does not itself parse the described
revision options so refer to the relevant Git man pages for further
information. Relevant man pages besides git-log(1) are git-diff(1) and
git-rev-list(1).

You can tune the interaction with Git by making use of the options explained
in this section. For example, by configuring the environment variable
described in the section on <<diff-options, diff options>>.

names, be sure to separate file names from other Git options using "`--`". So

        except: iw=0

        gc=self.opts.git_config.get('core.abbrev')
        if gc:
            try:
                v=int(gc); 
                if v>0: return v
            except: pass
        return 7
    def view_columns(self,name):
        key=name+'-view' if not name.endswith('-view') else name
        cols=self.opts.views.get(key)
        if cols is None:
            return parse_view_string("line-number text",key)
        # Return live list (toggles modify column opts)
        return cols
    # ---- repo / config loading order ----
    def load_config_files(self):
        loader=ConfigLoader(self.opts)
        # system
        sys_path=os.environ.get("TIGRC_SYSTEM")
        if sys_path is None:
            sys_path="/etc/tigrc"
        if sys_path!="":
            loader.load_file(sys_path,quiet=True)
        # user
        user_path=os.environ.get("TIGRC_USER")
        if user_path is None:
            xdg=os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
            if xdg:
                user_path=os.path.join(xdg,"tig","config")
            else:
                cand=os.path.expanduser("~/.config/tig/config")
                if os.path.exists(cand):
                    user_path=cand
                else:
                    user_path=os.path.expanduser("~/.tigrc")
        if user_path:
            loader.load_file(os.path.expanduser(user_path),quiet=True)

        if not args:
            self._parsed_files=[]; self._parsed_flags=[]; self._parsed_revs=[]; return True
        # Filter ??? Original passes most; keep as passed except maybe long special? We'll pass all.
        rc1,out1,err1=git_text(["rev-parse","--no-revs","--no-flags"]+args)
        if rc1!=0:

    # ----- Display building -----
    def build_virtual_display(self):
        # For headless/save-display: build lines based on size
        if getattr(self,'no_display',False):
            W,H=self._headless_size
        else:
            H,W=self.stdscr.getmaxyx() if self.stdscr else (24,80)
        self.last_display=self.render_display_lines(W,H)
        return self.last_display
    def render_display_lines(self,W,H):
        # Returns list of (plain_text, segments_per_row?, kind) - we keep plain strings plus structured rows for curses
        rows=[]
        # Determine layout
        layout=self.compute_layout(W,H)
        self._layout=layout
        # layout: list of pane dicts {view, x,y,w,h, title_y or title_x etc}
        # Build a grid of rows strings: first create empty rows H-1 (excluding status)
        grid=[[] for _ in range(max(0,H-1))]  # list of segment lists per screen row
        plain_grid=[""]*max(0,H-1)
        # For virtual/plain, we need to stitch panes horizontally for vertical split
        # We'll produce plain strings in grid_text list
        grid_text=[""]*max(0,H-1)
        for pane in layout['panes']:
            view=pane['view']; px=pane['x']; py=pane['y']; pw=pane['w']; ph=pane['h']
            view._pane_height=ph; view._pane_width=pw
            # ensure offset keeps selected visible
            self.ensure_visible(view,ph)
            for i in range(ph):
                idx=view.offset+i
                y=py+i
                if y<0 or y>=len(grid_text): continue
                if idx < len(view.lines):
                    line=view.lines[idx]
                    segs=view.segments(line,pw)
                    # apply xoffset and create plain
                    plain=self.segments_to_plain(segs)
                    # horizontal scroll: truncate by width starting xoffset, preserving glyphs (plain string slicing by characters approximate)
                    plain_disp=self.clip_plain(plain,view.xoffset,pw)
                    is_sel=(idx==view.selected)
                else:
                    plain_disp=""; is_sel=False
                # stitch
                existing=grid_text[y]
                # pad existing to px
                if len(existing)<px: existing=existing+" "*(px-len(existing))
                # if vertical split pane second overwrites at px
                grid_text[y]=existing[:px]+plain_disp.ljust(pw)[:pw] if layout['orientation']=='vertical' and px>0 else (plain_disp if px==0 and layout['orientation']!='vertical' else existing[:px]+plain_disp.ljust(pw)[:pw])
                # For vertical, titles will be added later at same row
                # store structured info for curses
                if not hasattr(self,'_row_info'): self._row_info={}
                self._row_info[(y,px)]={'view':view,'line_idx':idx if idx<len(view.lines) else None,'selected':is_sel,'pane':pane,'plain':plain_disp}
            # title row
            title_text,percent=self.make_title(view,ph,pw)
            if layout['orientation']=='vertical':
                ty=H-2
                existing=grid_text[ty]
                if len(existing)<px: existing=existing+" "*(px-len(existing))
                grid_text[ty]=existing[:px]+title_text.ljust(pw)[:pw]
            else:
                ty=py+ph
                if 0<=ty<len(grid_text): grid_text[ty]=title_text
            pane['title_text']=title_text; pane['title_y']= (H-2 if layout['orientation']=='vertical' else py+ph)
        # Trim trailing spaces for content rows but keep title rows – build_virtual expects original behaviour stored later.
        result=grid_text
        self._grid_text=result
        return result
    def compute_layout(self,W,H):
        focused=self.focused or self.current
        panes=[]
        orientation='horizontal'
        if len(self.display_views)>1:
            vs=str(self.opts.get('vertical-split','auto')).lower()
            if vs in ('yes','true','1'): orientation='vertical'
            elif vs in ('no','false','0'): orientation='horizontal'
            elif vs=='auto':
                # auto depends on dimensions: tig uses vertical if width is large relative to height? Probe later: choose vertical if W>160 and W>=4*H? We'll use aspect >= (?)
                orientation='vertical' if W>=180 else 'horizontal'
            else: orientation='horizontal'
            if orientation=='vertical':
                # width of right view split-view-width 50%
                wpct=self.percent_value(self.opts.get('split-view-width','50%'),W)
                right_w=max(4,min(W-4, wpct))
                left_w=W-right_w
                # views order display_views[0] left, [1] right
                panes=[{'view':self.display_views[0],'x':0,'y':0,'w':left_w,'h':H-2},{'view':self.display_views[1],'x':left_w,'y':0,'w':right_w,'h':H-2}]
            else:
                bottom_h=self.percent_value(self.opts.get('split-view-height','67%'),H-1)
                # bottom content height as percent of H-1? earlier derivation
                bottom_h=max(4, min(H-1-2-4, bottom_h)) if H>10 else bottom_h

                total_content=H-1-2
                if bottom_h>total_content-4: bottom_h=total_content-4

import subprocess,time,os
def capture(exe,cwd,args,keys=None,size=(80,24),env=None,wait=0.6):
    sess="scmp"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",sess],capture_output=True)
    envstr=""
    if env: envstr=" ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k,v in env.items())+" "
    cmd=f"cd {cwd} && {envstr}TERM=xterm-256color {exe} {args}; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 100"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",sess,"-x",str(size[0]),"-y",str(size[1]),cmd])
    time.sleep(wait)
    snaps=[]
    def snap():
        r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",sess,"-p"],capture_output=True,text=True)
        snaps.append(r.stdout)
    snap()
    if keys:
        for k in keys:
            if isinstance(k,(int,float)): time.sleep(k); snap(); continue
            if isinstance(k,list):
                for kk in k: subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,kk])
            elif isinstance(k,tuple) and k[0]=='lit':
                subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,"-l",k[1]])
                if len(k)>2 and k[2]: subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,"Enter"])
            else:
                subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess,k])
            time.sleep(0.3); snap()
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",sess],capture_output=True)
    return snaps

def compare(label,cwd,args,keys=None,size=(80,24),env=None):
    o=capture('/workspace/executable',cwd,args,keys,size,env)
    m=capture('/tmp/my_tig',cwd,args,keys,size,env)
    if o==m:
        print(f"OK {label}")
        return True
    print(f"DIFF {label} orig_snaps={len(o)} my_snaps={len(m)}")
    for i in range(max(len(o),len(m))):
        oo=o[i] if i<len(o) else "<missing>"; mm=m[i] if i<len(m) else "<missing>"
        if oo!=mm:
            print(f"--{label} snap{i} ORIG--"); print(oo); print(f"--{label} snap{i} MINE--"); print(mm)
    return False

            for line in b.splitlines():
                if line.startswith('commit '): c.id=line.split()[1]
                elif line.startswith('Reflog:'):
                    m=re.match(r'Reflog: (\\S+)',line)
                    if m: c._reflog_selector=m.group(1)
                elif line.startswith('Reflog message:'): c.subject=line[len('Reflog message:'):].strip()
                elif line.startswith('parent '): c.parents.append(line.split()[1])
                elif line.startswith('author '):
                    m=re.match(r'author (.*) (\\d+ [+-]\\d{4})$',line)
                    if m: c.author=m.group(1); c.adate=m.group(2)
                elif line.startswith('committer '):
                    m=re.match(r'committer (.*) (\\d+ [+-]\\d{4})$',line)
                    if m: c.committer=m.group(1); c.cdate=m.group(2)
                elif line.strip()=='': in_msg=True
                elif in_msg: msg.append(line.strip())
            if not c.subject: c.subject=msg[0] if msg else ""
            if not c.committer: c.committer=c.author; c.cdate=c.adate
            c.graph=""
            commits.append(c)
        self.commits=commits
        self.lines=[]
        for c in commits:
            vl=VLine(c.subject,commit=c.id,parents=c.parents); vl.data['commit_obj']=c; self.lines.append(vl)
    def title(self):
        l=self.current_line()
        if not l: return "[main]"
        c=l.data.get('commit_obj')
        sel=getattr(c,'_reflog_selector',None) if c else None
        info=sel if sel else l.commit
        return f"[main] {info} - commit {self.selected+1} of {len(self.lines)}"

        lines=view.lines; sel=view.selected
        cs=None
        for i in range(sel,-1,-1):
            if lines[i].text.startswith('@@'): cs=i; break
        if cs is None: return
        ce=len(lines)
        for i in range(cs+1,len(lines)):
            if lines[i].text.startswith('@@') or lines[i].text.startswith('diff --git'): ce=i; break
        # find context line separating changes
        split_idx=None
        has_change_before=False
        for i in range(cs+1,ce):
            txt=lines[i].text

            elif txt.startswith(' ') and has_change_before:

                    split_idx=i; break

            return

        o=old_start; n=new_start
        for i in range(cs+1,split_idx):
            txt=lines[i].text
            if txt.startswith('-'): o+=1
            elif txt.startswith('+'): n+=1
            elif txt.startswith(' '): o+=1; n+=1
        first_old=sum(1 for vl in lines[cs+1:split_idx+1] if not vl.text.startswith('+'))
        first_new=sum(1 for vl in lines[cs+1:split_idx+1] if not vl.text.startswith('-'))
        second_old=sum(1 for vl in lines[split_idx:ce] if not vl.text.startswith('+'))
        second_new=sum(1 for vl in lines[split_idx:ce] if not vl.text.startswith('-'))
        lines[cs].text=f"@@ -{old_start},{first_old} +{new_start},{first_new} @@{suffix}"
        new_header=VLine(f"@@ -{o},{second_old} +{n},{second_new} @@{suffix}")
        new_header.file=lines[split_idx].file

        lines.insert(split_idx+1,new_header); lines.insert(split_idx+2,dup)
        for idx,vl in enumerate(lines): vl.lineno=idx+1

        if not isinstance(view,StageView): return
        lines=view.lines; sel=view.selected

        for i in range(sel,-1,-1):
            if lines[i].text.startswith('@@'): cs=i; break
        if cs is None: return
        ce=len(lines)
        for i in range(cs+1,len(lines)):
            if lines[i].text.startswith('@@') or lines[i].text.startswith('diff --git'): ce=i; break
        # find context line separating changes
        split_idx=None
        has_change_before=False
        for i in range(cs+1,ce):
            txt=lines[i].text
            if txt.startswith('+') or txt.startswith('-'): has_change_before=True
            elif txt.startswith(' ') and has_change_before:
                # ensure change after
                if any(lines[j].text.startswith(('+','-')) for j in range(i+1,ce)):

            return
        m=re.match(r'@@ -(\\d+)(?:,(\\d+))? \\+(\\d+)(?:,(\\d+))? @@(.*)',lines[cs].text)
        if not m: return
        old_start=int(m.group(1)); new_start=int(m.group(3)); suffix=m.group(5)
        # position of split line
        o=old_start; n=new_start
        for i in range(cs+1,split_idx):
            txt=lines[i].text
            if txt.startswith('-'): o+=1
            elif txt.startswith('+'): n+=1
            elif txt.startswith(' '): o+=1; n+=1
        first_old=sum(1 for vl in lines[cs+1:split_idx+1] if not vl.text.startswith('+'))
        first_new=sum(1 for vl in lines[cs+1:split_idx+1] if not vl.text.startswith('-'))
        second_old=sum(1 for vl in lines[split_idx:ce] if not vl.text.startswith('+'))
        second_new=sum(1 for vl in lines[split_idx:ce] if not vl.text.startswith('-'))

        new_header=VLine(f"@@ -{o},{second_old} +{n},{second_new} @@{suffix}")
        new_header.file=lines[split_idx].file
        dup=VLine(lines[split_idx].text); dup.file=lines[split_idx].file; dup.commit=lines[split_idx].commit
        lines.insert(split_idx+1,new_header); lines.insert(split_idx+2,dup)
        for idx,vl in enumerate(lines): vl.lineno=idx+1
        self.status_message="Split the chunk in 2"
    # ----- save functions -----'''

    def _apply_chunk(self,view,reverse=False,cached=False):
        # Extract current chunk (from diff --git header of current file through next chunk/file) and apply to index/worktree.
        # Build patch text: headers for current file plus selected chunk
        lines=[vl.text for vl in view.lines]
        # find file header index <= selected
        sel=view.selected
        file_start=None; chunk_start=None
        for i in range(sel,-1,-1):
            if lines[i].startswith('@@') and chunk_start is None: chunk_start=i
            if lines[i].startswith('diff --git'): file_start=i; break
        if file_start is None: 
            # stage whole
            if view.only_file and not cached: run_git(["add","--",view.only_file],trace=False)
            return
        # header lines from file_start to chunk_start (exclusive) includes diff,index,---,+++
        if chunk_start is None: chunk_start=file_start
        # chunk ends at next @@ or diff --
        chunk_end=len(lines)
        for i in range(chunk_start+1,len(lines)):
            if lines[i].startswith('@@') or lines[i].startswith('diff --git'): chunk_end=i; break
        patch="\n".join(lines[file_start:chunk_start]+lines[chunk_start:chunk_end])+"\n"
        args=["apply","--cached"] if cached else ["apply"]
        if reverse: args.append("--reverse")
        # For unstaged staging a chunk, git apply --cached
        if not cached and view.section=='unstaged': args=["apply","--cached"]
        if cached and view.section=='staged': args=["apply","--cached","--reverse"]
        rc,out,err=run_git(args,input_data=patch.encode(),trace=False)

def run_trace(exe,args,cwd="/tmp/t1",script=":quit\n",stdin_data=None,env_extra=None,size=(200,50)):

    stdin_redir=""

    time.sleep(1.0)

    shown=[c for c in cols if is_column_shown(c)]
    non=[c for c in shown if c.type not in expanding_types]
    if not non or not pane_width: return widths
    total=sum(widths.get(c.type,0) for c in non)+(len(non)-1 if non else 0)
    # Reserve one column for delimiter/edge when truncating to fit before expanding column
    target=pane_width-1

    adj=dict(widths)

    for c in flex:
        if total<=target: break
        cur=adj.get(c.type,0)
        shrink=min(cur-1,total-target)

        self.status_message=f"Moving to parent is not supported by the {view.name} view"

                m=re.match(r'^(.*)\s+(\d+\s+[+-]\d{4})\s*$',s.strip())
